analysis.title: "It Was Gross": Goldman Says The AI Unwind Has Entered Phase Two As The $106 Billion Debt Bill Comes Due
key_insights: Goldman's Privorotsky says Thursday's selling shifted from net exposure to gross exposure. Global systematic L/S fell 1.4%, nearly a -4 sd move, with multi-sd squeezes in shorts alongside violent declines in longs, including through the European session. He calls this aggressive de-grossing.

As of Wednesday's close, Goldman Prime (Vincent Lin) had net leverage down 4.3 points month-to-date to 73.3%, the 6th percentile of the past year. Gross leverage was 310.3%, the 94th percentile over five years, and up 0.6 points in October. Funds cut bets, not balance sheets.
Goldman's Marco Laicini: Global Systematic L/S fell 1.4% (-3.7 SD), the worst day since Aug 19. Multi-strats running equity books at 4.5x leverage lost 1.2% (-2.2 SD).

Goldman's High Beta 12m Losers and Liquid Most Short baskets topped the leaderboard (Ariana Contessa) on a day the S&P closed up 33bps with a $5 billion sell MOC, indicating short covering rather than conviction buying.
Privorotsky said on Tuesday the selloff was rotation rather than wholesale liquidation because nets are conservative. The article notes nets were conservative but gross was not.
Goldman's broad AI basket (GSTMTAIP) is down 20% over five sessions, which the Asia sales desk places towards the lower end of recent unwind episodes.
KOSPI rose 2-3% overnight after losing nearly 20% over seven sessions. Privorotsky called the bounce a little lackluster relative to the scale of the selloff.

Goldman credit strategists (Amanda Lynam) report USD IG and HY project finance issuance year to date above $106 billion, nearly triple the $37 billion in 2025. Risks to the 2027 global forecast of $300 billion are skewed firmly to the upside.

HY datacenter bond prices fell from above $101 in June to nearly $95. Lynam's team sees neocloud and frontier-lab-exposed issuers as at the epicenter of the funding cost debate. The Asia sales desk says HY spreads are more than 150bp wider since mid-year because heavy supply can only be absorbed at higher yields.
Goldman credit stays underweight USD IG Technology but neutral on USD HY, citing scope for near-term reversal of the recent sell-off and more attractive valuations.

Privorotsky notes spot compute pricing remains very strong. B200, H200, H100 and even A100 rentals command meaningful rates. He sees undeniable scarcity of available compute, structurally bullish for owners. The Silicon Data B200 On-Demand Rental Index (non-hyperscale) printed 6.01, below March's 6.11 high and about 40% above January's 4.29 low.

Privorotsky suspects in hindsight this was a local low with credit-driven concerns locally overblown. He says there is too much capital seeking a home relative to the supply of investable, energized compute, and repricing may be gradual or acute, with potential to become systemic. Financing and electrification bottlenecks remain real.

Privorotsky calls hyperscalers perhaps the ultimate solution to funding concerns. He expects robust earnings and wonders if the FCF inflection could be pulled forward, reducing the need for incremental leverage. He also wonders whether selling hyperscalers versus semis becomes the relative trade.

Privorotsky says rates are beginning to reflect the AI capex growth shock. If AI capex disappoints, growth expectations fall and bonds rally. If spending meets expectations, yields probably go higher.

GS MarketStrats (Vitali Meschoulam) argues fiscal expansion and AI capex pushed real rates higher, and those rates now ration capital. AI may become one of the first casualties of rates already in place. The demand for capital may slow but the need for capital may not.

Privorotsky flags the primary dealer questionnaire ahead of the Nov 4 refunding. Some on the Street expect Treasury to cut 20Y and 30Y auction sizes by $3bn each, replacing supply with T-bills, with speculation the 20Y could be eliminated. Questions about cutting long-end supply would be bullish for duration, and no mention would likely disappoint.

Privorotsky is cautiously optimistic: choppy, but increasingly optimistic that much of the concern is priced into semis. The problem remains oil, which is stubbornly high. NDX forward P/E is about 21x per Goldman's US sales trading desk, the lowest since the AI cycle began in 2023.

ZeroHedge's own view: phase one (de-netting) is done and phase two (de-grossing) began Thursday. With gross at the 94th percentile there is further to go. WTI is near $98 and Goldman is tracking September core PCE at 3.12%.

tension_points.theme: AI compute scarcity vs financing stress
tension_points.bull_case: Spot rental pricing for B200, H200, H100 and A100 stays strong, with scarce energized compute structurally bullish for owners. Privorotsky suspects this was a local low and credit worries are locally overblown. Hyperscaler FCF could inflect early.
tension_points.bear_case: Project finance issuance is nearly triple last year, HY datacenter bonds are down about six points, HY spreads are 150bp wider since mid-year, and gross leverage at the 94th percentile leaves room for more de-grossing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler earnings that fail to pull forward the FCF inflection, or a Nov 4 refunding with no long-end supply cut.

theme_stances.key_argument: Selling shifted from net exposure to gross, with aggressive de-grossing across longs and shorts.
theme_stances.evidence: It was no longer about net exposure. It was gross.
